with that so the essential oils aren't so
strong." "And so we won't be allergic?" Jason asked.
"Yes. Some people get a rash from too much strong essential oil," Mr. Dunn said.
"So we're going to carefully measure how
much we put in." Everyone poured in the olive oil. Next Mr. Dunn
held up a bottle. "See this bottle's special top?
The dropper helps us measure the eucalyptus oil one drop at a time." Mr. Dunn put a
few drops in his hand. Then he rubbed his hands together and held
them up for the kids to smell.
"I like it," Izzie said. "It smells clean
and fresh." Ethan took a
sniff. "Wow! That's strong." "Put twenty drops into your bottle," Mr. Dunn said. Jason squinted.
"I feel like it might sting my eyes," he said. "The
oil could sting your eyes!" Mr. Dunn said. "So be very careful not to touch your eyes
after handling essential oils." "What do
we put in next?" Bobby asked.
Mr. Dunn held up
another bottle. "Citronella essential
oil." "We have citronella candles in our backyard," Nina said.
"Citronella keeps mosquitoes away," Mr. Dunn said. "So add twenty drops of this too.
Shake it up and you're done! Next time we go
on a hike, you can spray it on your arms and legs." "Try this if
you go outside tonight, Jason. I don't think any
mosquitoes will bother you," Mr. Dunn said.
"I'll try it," Jason
said. "But after last night, I have no skin left
to bite anyway!" Things you'll need: -a spray
bottle, about 90 ml -2 tablespoons olive oil
-eucalyptus essential oil -citronella essential oil -a
dropper for measuring Do it Yourself: 1) Pour the olive oil into the spray bottle. 2) Add 20
drops of eucalyptus essential oil. 3) Add 20 drops of
citronella essential oil. 4) Shake well. 5) Spray the mixture onto your
arms and legs and rub in
well. 6) Wash your hands, and then enjoy being outside without getting bitten by
mosquitoes!
"Bye, Mom." Nina hugged her mother. They had
walked together to Kids Central Summer Camp today. "Bye, sweetie. I'll be
back with Aunt Sujong at three o'clock to pick you up," Nina's mom said. "Yay!" Nina's Aunt Sujong was arriving from Korea today.
She was going to stay at Nina's house for one week.
"I hope we make a craft today. Then I can give it to Aunt
Sujong," Nina thought. In the gym Mr. Dunn was
holding a box of strawberries. Izzie was trying to guess how many
strawberries were in it. "Twenty-two," Izzie said. "I bet there are twenty-two." "What do
you think, Nina?" Mr. Dunn asked. Nina looked in the box. "Are we making
food today?" she asked, disappointed. "We're not making a craft?"
"We're making smoothies!" Jason guessed. "Nope. But you'll like this
too," Mr. Dunn said. "We're making
strawberry jam," Mr. Dunn said. "Have any of you made
jam before?" "I haven't," Bobby said.
"But my mom has." "Soon you'll know
how to help her. It's easy," said Mr. Dunn. "First we
need to wash these strawberries. Ethan, will you wash
them please? You could count the berries too,"
Mr. Dunn said. "Thirty-two!" Ethan announced as the kids put on
their aprons. Bobby grinned. "You weren't even close,
Izzie!" "Chop, chop, chop." Nina cut off
green top after green top. "Boring, boring, boring,"
she said grumpily. When they were done, Mr.
Dunn put the strawberries into five bowls. He held up some
potato mashers. "Everyone, grab one of these." "All right!" Ethan cheered. "We're mashing
stuff!" "Ha-ha. This is fun!" Izzie pressed her masher
into the berries.
"And messy." Nina pointed to Izzie's arms. They were covered
in strawberry juice. "Terrific. Those berries look ready
to cook," said Mr. Dunn. "Cook? You cook the berries to make jam?" Nina asked.
"Yes, and the heat helps to melt
the sugar," Mr. Dunn explained. "Now empty
your bowls into this pot." "Then add one
and half cups of sugar," Bobby read. "And two tablespoons of lemon juice," Izzie
said. "Heat on low until the sugar melts," Jason
read. "How will we know when it melts?"
"The sugar is white now, right? When it melts, we won't be
able to see it anymore. It turns into clear liquid—syrup!" Mr. Dunn explained.
Nina peeked into the pot. "I can see it melting!" "Now turn up that stove
and let it boil!" Mr. Dunn said. "Don't forget
to stir." Jason handed Nina a wooden spoon. "It's a pretty color,"
Nina said, stirring. "I think we can pour the jam
into the jars now," Mr. Dunn said soon. "Then we'll let
the jars cool and put them in the refrigerator."
A few hours later, Mr. Dunn took the
jam jars out of the refrigerator. "We have some ribbons and cards. You can
decorate your jar and give it to someone sweet," he
said. "Give it to someone?" Nina
thought. Suddenly she smiled. At the
end of the day, Nina ran to greet her mom and aunt. "Aunt Sujong!" she
cried. "This jam is for
you." "Thanks, Nina," Aunt Sujong said, hugging her.
Then she read Nina's card. It said: "Something
sweet for someone sweet." Things you'll need: -4 cups strawberries -a large bowl -a potato masher or a large
fork -1 ½ cups white sugar -2 tablespoons lemon juice -clean jam jars Do it
Yourself: 1) Wash the strawberries and cut off the green tops. 2) Place the strawberries in a large
bowl and mash them with a potato
masher or a large fork. 3) Mix the strawberries, sugar, and lemon juice in a pot. 4)
Heat on low until the sugar melts.
5) Turn up the
heat and bring to a boil. Cook for about twenty minutes, or until the mixture thickens. Stir often.
6) Remove from heat and
pour the jam into clean jam
jars. Let the jars cool. 7) Place the jam
jars in the refrigerator for a
few hours. 8) Eat with toast or yogurt and
enjoy!

episodes.title: Friendship Bracelets for Girls and Boys

subtitle.text: Izzie saw Ethan in the hallway ahead of her. She thought
he was nicer than the other boys. She hoped they could be
partners at Kids Central Camp one day. In the gym Mr. Dunn was sitting at
a table. "What's the string for?" Ethan asked. "Today we're making friendship
bracelets," Mr. Dunn said. "Friendship bracelets," Izzie thought.
"I could make one for—" "Bracelets are for girls!" said
Bobby. "No, they're not," Ethan
said. "At my school in California
everyone wore them." "Well, my sister and her
friends wear friendship bracelets," Bobby said.
"I think they're goofy." "They are not goofy," Mr. Dunn
said. "They're part of a meaningful tradition." He looked at Bobby. "When a friend
gives you a bracelet, you
should never cut it off. You wear it for
as long as the two of you remain
friends." "I can't wait to
make mine!" said Izzie. "First choose three colors," Mr. Dunn instructed. "This is pretty." Izzie reached
for a bundle of blue thread. But her hand bumped into another hand reaching for the
same one. "Sorry," Ethan mumbled. "I'll pick a different one." "You
can choose the same color," Mr. Dunn said.
"Izzie, measure out sixty
centimeters, and then give Ethan the thread." Everyone measured and
cut six strands of thread. Then Mr. Dunn showed them what to do. "Now tie
a knot ten centimeters from one end. Next tape that
end to the table. After that separate the strands by color. There
should be two strands of each color." "Now we're ready to weave!" said Nina.
Mr. Dunn nodded. "Start with the strand all the way
to the left. Use it to tie a knot around
the string next to it. Keep going all the way across.
Once you've knotted each string, start again on the
left. Do you understand?" Mr. Dunn asked. "Yep!" Izzie
said. This looked like it would take a while. She
wanted to finish hers today. "Weave away! Ask me
if you need help," said Mr. Dunn. "I'm making mine for you," Nina whispered to Izzie.
Izzie looked at her friend and swallowed. "Thanks." Then she got back to work. Knot,
knot, knot. Knot, knot, knot. Start again. Finally
she was done. Izzie's hands were cramping and her neck hurt from
bending over. But her bracelet looked great. "Okay,
campers. Time to get
out into that sunshine and play some kickball," Mr. Dunn
said. "If you're not done with your
bracelets, you can finish them at home," Mr. Dunn added. He leaned over and
looked at Izzie's bracelet. "Nice job, Izzie," he said. "You worked hard
today." "Thanks," said Izzie. She was glad she
was finished. When everything was put away, the kids
lined up to go outside. Izzie was behind Ethan at
the end of the line.
She saw Ethan stuff his unfinished bracelet in his pocket. "Hey, Ethan." Izzie poked
his arm. "I made my bracelet for
you. Will you wear it?" she mumbled. "Sure. Thanks, that's really nice," he told Izzie. "Cool." Grinning, Izzie tied the
bracelet on his wrist. Then she ran to the blacktop. Things you'll need: -three different colors of embroidery thread, about
60 centimeters each -a ruler or measuring tape -scissors -strong
tape Do it Yourself: 1) Cut
two strands of each color
of thread. Make sure
each strand is 60 centimeters long. 2) Tie
the six strands together by making a knot at one end. 3) Tape the knotted
end to a table or hard surface. 4) Begin with the string
at the left. Use it to tie a knot around the string directly
to its right. 5) Repeat with each string.
Then go back to the string at
the left and start again. 6) When there
are only 10 centimeters of loose string left, tie another
knot. 7) Give your friendship bracelet to a friend. If you
want, you can make a matching one for
yourself!

episodes.title: Leaves of Three, Let Them Be

subtitle.text: Ethan was having a great afternoon. The
Kids Central campers were on a nature hike in the woods. And Ethan loved
the woods. Mr. Dunn was showing
them moss and different kinds of wildflowers. "What's this?" Ethan asked, pointing to
a small yellow flower. "That's a buttercup," Nina said. "It's so
cute." "We're not touching anything today," Mr. Dunn called out
sternly. "We're just observing—from the trail, Ethan!" "Ha-ha, Ethan!" Bobby teased
him. "You got in trouble!" The next
day Mr. Dunn asked everyone to
draw a flower from the
nature hike. "Hey, Ethan. What's on your leg?" Izzie pointed to red welts on Ethan's legs. Ethan
was scratching like crazy. "I don't know.
But it's so itchy," Ethan said. "Uh-oh. It looks like
you've got poison ivy," Mr.
Dunn said. "Are we
going to get it too?" Jason backed
away from Ethan. "Jason, you probably don't have to worry. But Ethan was
wandering off the trail yesterday," Mr. Dunn said.
"Sorry, Mr. Dunn," Ethan mumbled. "I
should have stayed with the rest of the
group." Mr. Dunn nodded. "The oil from the poison ivy plants must have
gotten on your skin." "Oil?" said
Jason. "What oil?" "Plants have oil?" Nina asked. "It sounds like
you campers need to learn about poison ivy," Mr. Dunn said. "Let's visit the library. We can look up
facts about poison ivy. You can
finish your pictures later." Mr. Dunn
led the kids into the empty school library. "We'll research on the computers!" the boys said.
"We'll look for books," Izzie
and Nina said. Mr. Dunn called Ethan's mom to
tell her about the rash. Then he
gave Ethan an ice pack for his itchy leg. It helped a
little bit. An hour later the kids gathered on
the rug. "Who wants to share what you found
out?" Mr. Dunn asked. Bobby raised his hand. "I found out that poison
ivy is a plant with an oil that causes a rash." "You can
get the rash from touching the
plant or touching something that touched the plant. Like your
shoes," Bobby explained. "Or your pet." "That's absolutely right," Mr. Dunn said. "You
might not see the rash
until the next day," Jason added. "Right again. The rash usually doesn't appear until 12 to 48 hours
later," Mr. Dunn said. "And not everyone gets it." "We found some pictures of the rash." Nina held up
a book. "We also found out how to treat
it. Put anti-itch cream and calamine lotion
on it, and take cold, oatmeal baths," Izzie said. Jason looked through the first
aid kit. "I found calamine lotion!" "I have to put that pink stuff on me?" Ethan said unhappily. "Here's
what the poison ivy plant looks
like. So we can all avoid it when
we see it." Izzie showed them
pictures. "There's a special saying to help you remember:
Leaves of three, let them be," Mr. Dunn said. "Too bad I didn't know all this before," Ethan
said. "I'm itchy. I have to take cold
oatmeal baths. And I have
to put on pink lotion—ugh! I'll stay on the trail from now on!" Things
You Need: -an ice pack -calamine lotion -anti-itch cream
-oatmeal bath treatment What to Do If You Get a Poison Ivy
Rash: 1) Wash your
hands and the affected area with soap and water. 2)
Place an ice pack over the affected skin. 3) Pat
the skin dry, and then apply calamine lotion or anti-itch cream. 4)
If you're really itchy, you can take a bath in
oatmeal. 5) Try not to scratch! (And in the future,
do your best to avoid places where poison ivy
grows!)
Izzie hurried into the gym with her beach bucket. It was her
first day back at camp after vacation. "Should we hide these?" she asked
Mr. Dunn. "Before everyone else gets here?" He looked into the
bucket of seashells. "Yep. Let's go!" Izzie
and Mr. Dunn went out to the playground. They
hid Izzie's shells under
the swings and behind the soccer goals. They hid more shells around
the basketball nets and trees. They finished just as the other campers arrived. On the blacktop Mr.
Dunn explained the day's activity. "Today you'll hunt for secret treasures. I can't
tell you what they are." "Then how are we supposed to
find them?" Bobby asked. Mr. Dunn grinned. "I'll give you a clue.
The treasures are from the sea. When you've
found five items, bring them to the table." "Yeah,"
Izzie added. "We're going to make something cool!" "Good luck!" Mr. Dunn waved the
hunters off. "That clue wasn't very helpful," Jason complained. "Yes
it was. I know what we're hunting for,"
Bobby bragged. "I figured it out!" Just then Nina shouted, "I found something!" The
boys ran to Nina,
who was by the swings. "Watch where you
step!" she squealed. "They're delicate!" "What are?" Jason asked. Nina opened
up her hands. "The seashells." Once the campers knew
what they were looking
for, the seashells were easy to find. Soon they were all
at the table. "We've got
our seashells," Ethan said. "Now what?" "Well," Mr. Dunn said,
"Izzie kindly collected these seashells from the beach for us. And her dad
drilled tiny holes in each one. So I'll let her explain
today's craft." Izzie beamed proudly.
"We're making sea-breeze wind chimes." She held up a
chime. "My family made this one last year. It has four shells and one piece of sea glass. And this is
real driftwood." "What's driftwood?" asked Bobby. "Wood that's been
floating in the sea for a while," said Ethan. "I brought
you guys some driftwood too," Izzie added. "Thanks," Nina said. "How do we make the chimes?" "It's easy.
You just have to tie everything to the wood," Izzie said. "First we
have to make the hanger. Cut a piece of
string about sixty centimeters
long. Tie one end of the string
around one end of your stick.
Then tie the other end of the string to the
other end of the stick. Now we're ready to attach the shells to
the chime. Cut five pieces of string
about thirty centimeters long each.
Thread one string through the hole in one shell and knot it. Then tie the other
end of the string to the driftwood. Keep doing this until all
your shells are hanging
down from the wood." The campers laid out
their shells, cut string, and got to work. "Make sure the knots are tight," Mr. Dunn said. "Hey,
Izzie, thanks," Ethan said. "This reminds me of the
beach in California." "You're welcome," Izzie said. She tied a small pink
scallop shell to her wind chime and smiled. Today she shared a fun part of her
beach vacation with her friends. And that felt as cool as a sea breeze! Things you'll need: -about five seashells with
tiny holes drilled in them -a skinny piece of driftwood or a stick
-about 250 centimeters of string -scissors Do it Yourself: 1) Collect seashells at
the beach or purchase them from a craft store. 2) Ask an adult to drill a tiny
hole in each seashell. 3) Find a piece of driftwood or a regular stick.
A skinny stick about thirty to forty centimeters works best. 4) To make the chime's hanger, cut a
piece of string about sixty centimeters long. 5) Tie one end of the string to one
end of the stick. 6) Tie the other end of the string
to the other end of the stick.
7) To hang the shells, cut five pieces of string
about thirty centimeters long. 8) Thread
one end through the hole in a seashell. Tie the other end around your stick. Repeat until
all your seashells have been added to the chime. 9) Hang your sea-breeze wind chime on your porch
or by a window. Think of the beach every time the wind
blows!
The Kids Central summer campers were eating lunch outside. But Jason
wasn't eating. "What's the
matter, Jason?" Mr. Dunn asked. "You're not hungry today?"
"I'm hungry," Jason said,
poking at his zucchini. "But I'm really sick of zucchini.
We have a lot of it in
our garden now. My mom makes me eat it every day!" Mr.
Dunn looked shocked. "Really? You're sick of zucchini?" "I
love zucchini," said Bobby. "It's
not that bad," Izzie added. "Just
eat it, Jason." "No wait—don't!" Mr.
Dunn suddenly covered Jason's zucchini with his
hand. Everyone stared at
Mr. Dunn. "What's
wrong?" asked Jason. "I just remembered," said Mr. Dunn. "We're
making something today that might help
you enjoy the zucchini!" Mr.
Dunn started cleaning up his lunch. "I'm
going to grab our supplies," he said. "Can I help?" Jason asked. "Sure.
You can help me carry some things," Mr.
Dunn said. In the gym Mr. Dunn picked up two
bags. He pointed to the long
extension cord and blender on the table. "Can you carry those things?" he
asked. "Sure." Jason picked them up and followed Mr. Dunn
outside. "We're going to make a magic dip," Mr. Dunn said. "It will help
you eat zucchini and other vegetables you don't like."
Ethan made a sour face. "Even cauliflower?" he asked. "Absolutely cauliflower,"
Mr. Dunn answered. "What's in the magic dip?" Ethan asked. "Jason, please
show us what's in the grocery bag." Mr. Dunn set the bags on the
table. "Olive oil and roasted almonds,"
Jason said, pulling two items
out of the bag. "A lemon
and garlic cloves." "That's it?" Ethan asked, surprised.
"Nope," said Jason. "Here's salt and pepper too." "Boys," said Mr.
Dunn, "can you squeeze the lemon to make three
tablespoons of juice? Girls, can you
measure one-third cup of olive oil?" Mr. Dunn plugged in the
blender. "We can put in everything
at once," he said. "Roasted almonds,
garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil." Whrr ! The
blender hummed and spun. "Now let's add a little salt and pepper," said Mr. Dunn. "Nice and creamy,"
said Izzie. "Perfect for our dip," said Mr. Dunn. He
spooned some dip onto a plate and
handed it to Jason. "Now try your zucchini." Everyone watched Jason
dip a zucchini stick into the dip. "Well?" Izzie
burst out. "Do you like it?" Jason squeezed
his eyes as he chewed the zucchini. "Yes!" he cried at last. "It's
good. Try some!" he told
everyone. "Success!" said Bobby. "Jason, what should we name
our magic dip?" asked Mr. Dunn. "Kids Central Summer Dip," Jason said. "But I'm
going to make this at
home too!" Things you'll need: -1/3 cup roasted almonds -2 garlic
cloves -3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice -1/3 cup olive oil
-dash of salt and pepper -blender -fresh vegetables such as
zucchini, carrots, and cauliflower for dipping
Do It Yourself: 1) Combine the first four ingredients
in a blender
and blend until smooth and creamy. 2) Add a dash of salt and
pepper and stir. 3) Transfer the dip
to a bowl. 4) Dip in your favorite summer vegetables, and
enjoy!
Ethan's stomach was growling. He
had been hungry all day, even after eating lunch. Mr. Dunn clapped his hands.
"All right, campers. Let's clean up and
head outside." The kids
put away their art things and followed Mr.
Dunn outside. "You've all played tic-tac-toe, right?" he said. Everyone nodded. "And normally you play on
paper, right?" Everyone nodded again. "Well, today we will play
a 3-D
version of tic-tac-toe." "What does 3-D mean?" Nina asked. "It's
when something isn't flat
like a drawing on a piece of paper," Jason explained. "If something has
height, width, and depth, it's three-dimensional, or 3-D.
Like us!" "Right," Mr. Dunn said. "Today instead of drawing X 's and O 's for tic-tac-toe, you'll toss beanbags." He
showed them the beanbags. They were lumpy sacks tied at the top. "The blue ones have X
's on them, and the white
ones have O 's." "Did you make those?" Izzie asked. Mr. Dunn smiled. "Yes, I did.
Last night." Izzie nodded. "They look homemade."
"What's in them?" Ethan wanted to know. "We'll find out
at the end of the game," said Mr. Dunn. "Now who wants to play first?" Bobby and Izzie
raised their hands. "Okay, you two, stand behind
this line. Bobby, you can be X , and Izzie, you'll
be O ." "You can go first,"
Bobby told Izzie. "Thanks," she said. She tossed her
beanbag to the far-right corner of the board. Bobby went next. He tossed his bag to
the space beneath her bag. Ethan noticed two
more beanbags by Mr. Dunn's feet. "Are those extra
beanbags?" he asked. Mr. Dunn nodded. "In case one
gets ripped." He turned back to the board. "Nice play, Izzie!" he said,
clapping. Izzie had gotten her three O 's in a
row. "I win!" she
cried. "The winner gets to play again. Who wants to challenge Izzie?" Mr. Dunn asked.
"I do!" said Jason.
He stepped up to the line. "You can go first," Izzie said. "Since
I'll probably win." Jason rolled his eyes and tossed his beanbag onto the
board. Meanwhile Ethan picked up an extra beanbag.
The beans inside felt a little soft. They were definitely not
regular beans. Ethan sniffed the bag. "I knew
it!" he thought. "Tic-tac-toe, three in a row!"
Izzie cried. "Nina, it's your turn!" As Nina stepped up to the
line, Ethan untied the beanbag.
He emptied it into his mouth. "Oh no!"
Nina cried. "This bag has a hole in it!" "Don't worry,
we have extra bags. And no
peeking at the filling yet, Nina," Mr. Dunn
said. "Ethan, please toss me the extra O
bag." Ethan looked at the
empty beanbag in his hand. It had an O . "I can't, Mr. Dunn," said
Ethan. "I ate all the beans inside!" "Ethan!" Mr. Dunn
scolded him. "You didn't listen to me!" "But they
were jelly beans!" Ethan said. "Delicious jelly beans!"
"You ruined the game, Ethan!" Bobby
said. "That's okay," Izzie said quickly.
"Maybe it's time for a snack?" Mr. Dunn nodded. "Okay.
Jelly beans for everyone." "Even
Ethan?" asked Bobby. "Yes," Mr. Dunn said at last. He smiled. "Even Ethan!" Things You'll
Need: -jelly beans, about 900 grams -ten pieces
of cloth cut into squares, 25
x 25 centimeters (or twelve pieces, if you want
to make extras) -a fabric paint pen or
marker -string or ribbon -chalk Do It Yourself: 1) Mark five pieces of cloth with
a big X and five with a big O . 2)
Lay the pieces of cloth on a flat surface, with the marked
sides down. Fill the center
of each piece of cloth with jelly beans
(about two or three handfuls). 3) Gather the edges
of the cloth to form a
small bag. Tie the top tightly with
a string or ribbon. Repeat until you have made ten
bags. 4) Draw a
large tic-tac-toe board on the ground with chalk. 5)
Draw a line for players to stand
behind. 6) Players throw the beanbags onto the
board from behind the line. 7) The first player to line
up three bags in a
row wins. 8) Try not to eat any
jelly beans until after you finish
playing!
Nina was playing Frisbee at summer camp. But she
was thinking about Saturday. In just two days
her family would go to see the town fireworks. "Mr. Dunn, I love the Fourth of
July," Nina said. "Everything is red, white, and blue. And fireworks are so
cool." "The Fourth of July is fun, isn't
it?" Mr. Dunn said. "My family always
has a big barbecue. My dad and brothers love to grill." "My dad loves
to grill too!" Bobby said. "I always eat lots
of watermelon on the Fourth," Izzie said. "You know
what the kids in my family do on the Fourth?
They make red-white-and-blue ice pops. Then they eat them while watching fireworks," said Mr.
Dunn. "Red, white, and blue ice pops? I bet they're pretty," Nina said. "Yeah. They're pretty—and
pretty easy to make," Mr. Dunn
said, chuckling. "Can we make them at camp?" Nina asked. "Please? It's almost
the Fourth of July." Mr. Dunn smiled. "That's
a great idea, Nina. I'll bring in
everything we need tomorrow." The next day Mr. Dunn brought in paper cups, wooden craft
sticks, and three big bottles. Nina looked at the bottles.
"Ooh, red juice," she said. "That's sweet strawberry juice.
Made it myself," Mr. Dunn said. "Blue juice." Nina picked
up another bottle. "Grape-blueberry blend. That's cool. And white
juice. Wait a minute—white juice?" "It's actually coconut milk," Jason said, pointing to the label. "Have you had it before? It's
good." Nina shook her head. "But
I guess I'll try it in the
ice pops." "This will be
the easiest recipe you ever prepare," said Mr.
Dunn. "First pour some blue juice into the bottom
one-third of
the cup." "The juice has to freeze
before we can add the
next layer, right?" Jason asked.
"Exactly," said Mr. Dunn. "So let's get started."
The kids filled the bottom of their paper cups
with grape-blueberry juice. Then Mr.
Dunn took the cups to the freezer. "We'll take those out in two
hours," he said. The kids went outside for a nature walk. When they got back,
it was time for the next step. "Now add the coconut milk. Fill the middle one-third
of your cup," said Mr. Dunn. "And do it quickly. We don't want our blue to melt!" Mr. Dunn
hurried to get the ice pops back into the freezer.
Then the kids went outside for their Friday kickball tournament. In two hours they were back
inside, ready to finish making their ice pops. "Last step: strawberry
juice and craft sticks," Mr. Dunn said. "After you pour the strawberry
juice, put your sticks in the cup. The coconut milk
is still a little slushy. So you can gently push your stick through until
it stands up straight," Mr. Dunn said.
"Hurry, get these to the freezer!" Nina said. While they waited, Mr. Dunn
read them a book about
fireworks. Then they all painted fireworks. Finally the kitchen
timer went off. It was time to take out the ice pops! Mr. Dunn peeled
off the paper cups and handed a pop to each camper. "Yummy," Izzie
said, taking a lick of blue. Nina licked the white part. "The coconut milk is good! Thanks, Mr.
Dunn." Nina giggled. "Fourth-of-July fireworks, here I come!" Things you'll need: -paper or
plastic cups (about 236 ml) -wooden craft sticks -red juice (any flavor) -sweetened coconut milk
-blue juice (any flavor) Do It Yourself: 1) Fill one-third of
a small paper cup with blue juice. Put the cup in the freezer for at least two hours. 2) When
the blue juice has frozen, fill the next one-third of the
cup with coconut milk. Try to do this as quickly as possible. Put the
cup back in the freezer for
at least two more hours. 3) When the
coconut milk has frozen, fill the last one-third of the cup with
red juice. 4) Put the craft stick in your cup. Push it gently through the slushy center part
so that it stands up straight. Put the cup back
in the freezer for at least
two more hours. 5) When all the layers of your red-white-and-blue
ice pop are frozen, cut away the cup, and
enjoy!
Bobby couldn't stop grinning. It
was his birthday. Today at
one o'clock he would be ten years old. "Happy Birthday!" the other
campers called from the blacktop. "Thanks," Bobby said. "Where's the party?
Who's hiding the presents and cake?" Mr.
Dunn laughed. "Party? Presents? This is camp, not
a party center." "Oh." Bobby's grin
disappeared. "I was just kidding." He looked away.
"Sort of," he thought. All
morning the kids played kickball
on the blacktop. When
they went back inside,
Bobby was still thinking about his birthday. For Ethan's birthday they
had made special cupcakes with Miss Shelly. But they weren't doing anything for Bobby's birthday!
At twelve thirty Mr. Dunn made an announcement. "We're going out to the
soccer field. Please line up." "That's weird," Bobby thought, following
Mr. Dunn outside. "Mr. Dunn isn't carrying a soccer ball."
None of the other kids seemed to notice.
But when Bobby looked
at the soccer field, he was even more confused. There
were four tables on the field. A black
box sat on each one. "Birthday boy," Mr. Dunn called.
"Inside each box is a present from one of your friends. You must use your senses
to figure out what each one is. But you'll
be blindfolded." "If you can figure out what
is inside each box," Mr. Dunn
continued, "the presents are yours. Think you can do it?" Bobby grinned. He was
wrong. His friends had planned something special for his birthday! "Of course I can!"
he said. "Here's the blindfold,
Mr. Dunn," said Nina. She passed him a handkerchief, which he used to blindfold Bobby. Then Mr. Dunn led Bobby up
to the first box. "You have
to use your sense of touch
to guess what this present is," Mr. Dunn said. Bobby reached
into the box and felt something hard
and plastic. He pushed a lever and water shot
out. "A spray soaker!" he shouted. "You guessed it!" Izzie said. The kids
cheered. "Great job!" Mr. Dunn said. "Now, for box number two, you
have to use your sense of smell." Ethan lifted the present out of the box and held it under Bobby's nose.
Bobby sniffed. "I know this smell. A basketball!" he cried. "Right again! For
box number three you can use only your sense of
taste," Ethan said. Jason dipped a
spoon into box number three and
handed it to Bobby.
"Ice cream!" cried Bobby. "Yum. It
tastes like birthday cake!" Everyone cheered again. "For the last box, you have to use your
sense of hearing," said Mr. Dunn. "How can I hear a present?" asked Bobby. Nina opened box
number four. "I'm going to shake the
present a little and then
drop it on the table. Okay?" Nina said. Bobby nodded. Everyone got very quiet. What Bobby heard sounded like k-sh
, k-sh , k-plonk . "I'd know that sound anywhere. It's a box of sour lemon
balls—my favorite!" Bobby cried.
He removed his blindfold and smiled at his
friends. It was
one o'clock. "Happy Birthday, Bobby!" shouted everyone. Things You’ll Need: -a handkerchief -large boxes with lids -pen or marker
-a variety of items for the birthday child to
touch, taste, hear, and smell Do It
Yourself: 1) Place one item in each box and number each box. 2) Tie the handkerchief around the
birthday child to blindfold
him or her. 3) Tell the blindfolded
child that he or she can only use one sense
at a time to guess each
item. 4) Have someone carefully lead the blindfolded child to each box
and hand the item to him or her. 5) Have fun
watching the birthday child guess
what the item in each box
is!
Izzie squeezed Nina's hand and smiled. She
loved to go to the woods during summer camp. Today the campers had
a mission. They were looking for wildflowers!
"How do we know what to
pick?" Izzie asked. "We don't want to pick flowers growing on a
vine or bush. So look for flowers growing on the ground from one stem. Big
flowers with thick petals will be best," Mr. Dunn said. "Is this one
good?" Bobby asked. Bobby pointed to a white flower the size of a fingernail.
"No, silly," said Izzie. "You need something
bigger and darker, right, Mr. Dunn?" The teacher nodded. "Nina, look at this!" Izzie
squatted next to two purple
flowers. "Oh, they're so pretty! I love the color," Nina gushed.
"Can we pick these,
Mr. Dunn?" Izzie asked. "You may. Those look perfect," said Mr. Dunn. The
girls each picked one. "Here
are some!" Jason called. He pointed to the
same kind of flowers Izzie had found. But his were
bright yellow. And there were only three of them. Izzie
rushed over, pushing Jason aside. "Let
me get one!" "Izzie." She felt
a firm hand on her arm. "This is not a competition, and we do
not push," Mr. Dunn said. "Sorry."
Izzie watched grumpily as Jason, Ethan, and Bobby picked
their flowers. "Jackpot!" Ethan cried. He pointed
to a small circle of
color. It was made up of flowers—dark purple, light purple, and
yellow flowers! "You only need two flowers," Mr. Dunn said. "Don't pick more than that. Flowers
are living plants, and their home is here in nature." But Izzie ignored him. Quickly
she picked six flowers.
Back in the gym, everyone placed their flowers on the
table. Izzie had seven. Everyone else had two. "We're going to make hammered flower artwork,"
said Mr. Dunn. "I'll explain as we work. "I gave
everyone two pieces of watercolor paper.
So you can only use two flowers," said Mr. Dunn. He looked at
Izzie sharply, and then continued.
"Place one flower on the watercolor paper.
Then place a paper towel on top. Using your hammer, gently pound your
flower. Then lift up
the paper towel to see
what's left," Mr. Dunn continued. Izzie chose her favorite flower and began
pounding. When she pulled back her
paper towel, she gasped. "It looks like a stamp," Izzie
exclaimed. "But also like a painting!" Suddenly she felt bad for picking more
flowers than she needed. "Mr. Dunn?" she said. "I'm sorry
I didn't listen to you. Can I put
my extra flowers in water so they don't die
right away?" Mr. Dunn nodded. "I'm sure you'll be
a better listener next time," he said. "I'll put the flowers in water. You can keep
working on your hammered artwork. It looks great." "Thanks," said
Izzie. Izzie carefully picked off a piece of petal that was
stuck to the paper. Mr. Dunn was so nice.
Izzie knew just what to do
with her hammered artwork when it was ready. She was going to give it
to Mr. Dunn! Things
You'll Need: - one or more wildflowers (It's best
to use dark or brightly colored ones.) - newspaper - watercolor paper - paper towels - a hammer
- tweezers Do
It Yourself: 1) Cover your work surface with a sheet of newspaper. 2) Place
one flower on a sheet of watercolor
paper. 3) Cover the flower with a paper towel. 4)
Using your hammer, gently
pound the flower through
the paper towel. Check to make sure that the color is transferring to the watercolor paper. 5)
After you have hammered every part
of the flower, remove the paper towel. 6) If there are any flower bits stuck to your paper,
use tweezers to remove them. 7) Admire your amazing work of
art!
When Nina arrived at summer camp, Mr. Dunn was setting a basket of lemons on the picnic table. "Good morning, Mr. Dunn!"
she called. "Good morning, Nina," Mr. Dunn said.
Nina picked three lemons out of the
basket. Her aunt had tried to teach her how to
juggle last week. But Nina still couldn't do it. Plop, plop, plop. The lemons landed
on the ground. By now the other
campers arrived. "Hey, Nina!"
Bobby laughed. "Did you sign up for clown
school?" Nina frowned at him. "I'm not
a clown!" Izzie picked up
the lemons. "Do we need these lemons today?" Mr.
Dunn nodded. "It's okay that
they fell. We're going to
squeeze all of the juice out
of them anyway." "Yay! We're making lemonade!"
Izzie cried. Inside the gym the kids gathered around Mr.
Dunn. "Lemonade is one of my favorite summer drinks," the teacher said. "It's one of
mine too!" said Izzie. "I like it
really sweet." "Then you'll love this recipe," Mr. Dunn said. Ethan read
the board. "To make the syrup, we have to heat the sugar and
water until the sugar dissolves. But how will we
know when the sugar dissolves?" "It'll
disappear," said Mr. Dunn. "And turn into a clear syrup."
Ethan and Jason made the
syrup. The other campers cut lemons. Mr. Dunn handed forks to the lemon-cutters. "Now we remove the seeds." After Nina,
Izzie, and Bobby removed the seeds, they squeezed the lemons to
make juice. "Should we take out the pulp?" Nina asked. "No way!" Izzie cried.
"Pulpy lemonade is the best!" Soon the
syrup was cool, and the lemon
juice was ready. Bobby poured them both into the
pitcher. "Is that it?" he asked.
"Almost," Mr. Dunn said. "We made the sweet part. And we made the sour part. Now we have to
add water." "How much water?" Nina asked. "Let's start by
adding two and half cups. We'll keep tasting the lemonade until
it's just right," Mr. Dunn said. They each poured half a cup of
water into the pitcher. Izzie poured herself a little
lemonade. "Mmm. It's sweet!" Nina tried
a small sip. "It's too
sweet! Let's add more water." After
they added one more half cup of water,
Bobby tried the lemonade. "Mmm! That's good."
Ethan tasted some too. "I think
it needs more water. But only a little bit." "I
agree," said Jason. "Let's just add ice cubes now," Nina suggested. "Great idea!" said Mr.
Dunn. "Ice will cool the lemonade and add just a tiny bit of water."
He got ice cubes from a cooler
and added them to
the pitcher. Then everyone had a
glass of iced lemonade.
"Wow! This is better than
the lemonade at the deli," Izzie said. "This is good enough to sell!" Bobby said. "We
could have a Kids
Central Lemonade Stand!" Nina cried.
"Then instead of juggling lemons, I can
make lemonade!" To make about six
servings of lemonade you'll need:
- 1 cup white sugar - half cup cold water,
plus 3 cups cold water -
3/4 cup lemon juice and pulp (squeezed from about 6 lemons) - ice cubes Do It
Yourself: 1) Combine sugar and 1/2 cup water in a small pot. Heat until the sugar dissolves.
2) Remove the sugar syrup from the stove and
allow to cool. 3) Cut the lemons in half and remove the seeds. 4) Squeeze
the lemons until you have 3/4 cup of juice and
some pulp. 5) Combine the syrup, lemon juice and pulp, and 3 cups
of water in a large pitcher. 6) Add ice cubes and
enjoy!
Ethan looked at his permission slip. The campers
were going to Sunnydale Park today, but he didn't know why. Then Mr. Dunn solved the mystery. "The
Kite Festival is at the park today. And
we're going to participate!" "But we don't have kites," said Jason.
"Not yet. But we will soon," Mr.
Dunn said. "Are we going shopping for kites?" Izzie
asked. Mr. Dunn laughed. "We're going to make our kites, Izzie." Izzie cheered,
but Nina frowned. "That sounds hard," she said. "It's actually
very easy." Mr. Dunn pointed to the table. "If we attach strings and tails
to these paper bags, they should fly."
"That sounds fun," said Ethan. "Let's get
started." "First find the top
of your bag, where it opens," said Mr.
Dunn. "With masking tape, mark the four corners, two on each side. After that we'll punch a hole
in each corner." The kids marked the corners. Then they punched
the holes. "Now we need to add string to fly our kites," said Mr. Dunn. "Cut two pieces
of string 75 centimeters long. Thread one string through the left hole on one side
of the bag. Tie a knot so the string won't slip through."
"Then thread the other end of the
string through the right hole and
knot it," said Mr. Dunn. "Repeat on the other side." "Hey!" said Izzie. "I made two loops!" Next
Mr. Dunn told them how to make the handles. "Cut a
string 100 centimeters long. Pull it through the two loops you just made," Mr. Dunn continued. "And tie
the ends." Mr. Dunn checked everyone's handles. "Fantastic! Now we're ready to
decorate." "There will be lots of kites at the festival," said Mr. Dunn. "So paint your name in huge letters on your kite. After
that, cut up some streamers and glue
them to the bottom of your bag. Any questions?" Mr.
Dunn looked around. "Nope." Ethan had already started painting. "I like those polka
dots," said Izzie. "Very colorful!" "Thanks," said Ethan, adding
orange and yellow streamers to the bottom of the bag. "I want my kite to look
like a flaming comet!" After
lunch it was finally time to go
to the festival. "This looks really cool," Ethan
said, admiring his kite. He tucked it under his arm and lined up behind Mr. Dunn. Ethan
couldn't believe how crowded the park was. He didn't know there were so
many kite-lovers in Sunnydale! Mr. Dunn pointed to an empty patch of grass. "We can launch our kites over there," he
said. Ethan looked up. The sky was colorful
as kites flew in every direction. "I'm worried,"
Jason said. "Maybe our kites won't fly." "You won't know until you
try," Ethan said. "Come on!" He grabbed his kite's handle and started to run. "Yeah! Let's go!" Izzie grabbed
her kite and ran after Ethan. Both of their kites took off in the
wind. Ethan weaved through the crowd with his kite soaring. Everyone's kites were different, but
they all looked great. Soon he saw Jason following him. Jason's kite
was in the air too. "Doesn't it feel good to fly?" Ethan shouted. Things You'll Need:
- a brown paper grocery bag (without handles) - scissors -
masking tape - a hole puncher - about 250 centimeters of string - paint
or markers for decorating - crepe paper streamers - a glue stick
Do It Yourself: 1) With masking tape, mark four places to punch holes
along the top edges
of both sides of the bag. 2) Punch holes through the masking tape.
3) Cut two 75-centimeter pieces of string. 4) Thread one end of
one string through a hole on one side of the bag.
Knot the end. Then thread the other end of the string through the other hole
on the same side of the bag and knot it. Repeat on the other side
of the bag with the other piece of string. 5) Cut a 100-centimeter
piece of string. Thread it through the loops of string to form
a handle. 6) Decorate your kite with paint or markers. With glue
attach streamers to the bottom of the bag.
7) When your kite is dry, take it outside. Hold
the handle and run as fast as you can. Watch it
fly!
Bobby wiped the sweat off his forehead. It
was only nine o'clock, but it was already hot. He didn't mind.
Today was Three-Legged Race
Day! The Kids Central campers were
having three-legged races this morning. They were taking turns being partners
with each other. At the end of the day, they'd see
which team ran fastest. That team would win the blue ribbon! The five campers
gathered on the soccer field. "Please choose a partner
for your first race," Mr. Dunn called. "Want to
be partners?" Ethan asked Bobby. "Sure!" said Bobby. He knew Ethan would be
a fast partner. Bobby and Ethan tied their
inside legs together with
a scarf. "Practice walking first. Then try running," Mr.
Dunn suggested. Bobby was a little taller than Ethan, but it was easy
to walk together. "Ready?"
Mr. Dunn asked. The kids lined up.
Bobby and Ethan were racing against Nina and Izzie. "On your mark, get set, go!" "One, two.
One, two. One, two,"
Bobby and Ethan chanted as
they easily ran ahead of the girls. "With a time of
32 seconds, the winners are Bobby and
Ethan!" Mr. Dunn called. Next Bobby teamed
up with Jason. They raced against Nina and Ethan. But Bobby and Jason tripped
a lot. "With a time of 34 seconds, the winners are Nina and Ethan!" Mr. Dunn announced. In
the third race, Bobby was partners with
Nina. But she was a lot shorter
than him. And they couldn't stop falling! "With a
time of 36 seconds, the winners are Jason and Izzie! There are just two more races. Can
anyone beat Bobby and Ethan's record of 32 seconds?" Mr. Dunn
challenged the campers. "I bet I can," Izzie said. "Let's
be partners!" Bobby said to
Izzie. They quickly tied their legs together. "We can beat you," said Ethan, who was
paired up with Jason. "Jason and I
are almost the same height. So we're going to be fast." Ethan
was right about being fast. As
soon as Mr. Dunn said "Go!" the
two boys shot ahead. "One, two. One, two.
One, two. One, two," Izzie and Bobby
grunted. They went faster and
faster. Izzie and Bobby fell down just as they
crossed the finish line. "With a time of 31 seconds,
Izzie and Bobby have become the fastest
pair!" Mr. Dunn cried. Bobby wiped grass
off his T-shirt and grinned at Izzie. "Only one more race to go. Nina
and Jason versus Izzie and Ethan," said Mr. Dunn. "Oh no. I still have
another race!" Izzie said, trying to
catch her breath. Bobby watched nervously as the racers lined up. "On your mark, get
set, go!" Mr. Dunn called. Nina and Jason stumbled while Izzie and Ethan zoomed ahead. Were they fast enough to
beat Bobby and Izzie's time? "With a time of 32 seconds, Izzie
and Ethan do not beat the record.
The winners are Izzie and Bobby!" Mr. Dunn announced. "You are
the fastest girl I know," Bobby said. Izzie grinned.
"Thanks. Now let's race to get our blue
ribbons!" Things You'll Need: - some long scarves - two
long ropes Do It Yourself! 1) Use one rope for
the starting line and the other rope for the finish line. 2)
Divide into pairs. Try to find a partner that is the same
height as you. 3) Stand next to each other and tie your inside legs together with
a scarf. 4) Line up at the starting line. 5) The
first pair to make it to the finish line wins! 6)
Play again.
The pair with the fastest time of all is the final
champion!
Jason walked into the gym and bumped into a tall, young woman. "Ooph!" "Jason, I'd like you
to meet Allison. She's from Penny's Dog Shelter," said Mr.
Dunn. "Penny's Dog Shelter?" Jason was excited. "My mom and
I like to visit the dogs there. My
favorite one is Lucy. But we can't adopt her. My dad is allergic."
Allison smiled. "I'm sure Lucy enjoys your
visits." "And guess what!" cried Izzie. "We're
going to visit the shelter
tomorrow!" "Yeah," added Ethan. "Allison is going to show us how
to make dog treats. We can
bring them to the dogs tomorrow." "We're making peanut butter
treats," said Allison. "Because
almost all dogs love peanut butter. These treats are really easy to make. They
only have four ingredients!" "Peanut butter and . . . ?"
Izzie began to guess. "And water, whole wheat flour,
and oats," said Allison. "Can you preheat the oven
to 175 degrees, Mr. Dunn?" "Yes," said Mr. Dunn. "First
we mix the dry ingredients in
a large bowl," said Allison. "We need two cups of flour and one cup of
oats." Ethan and Bobby measured the dry ingredients. "Now we have to
spray the measuring cup with oil," Allison said." So the peanut butter will
come out more easily!" Mr.
Dunn knew what to do next. "Nina, can you please get one and a quarter cups
of hot water?" Jason dumped the peanut butter into a bowl. Then Nina added the
hot water while Jason stirred. "Now let's add the
peanut butter mix to the dry mix," said Allison. "Combine until it becomes a nice dough
ball." Izzie started kneading the mixture. Next Allison held up a rolling
pin. "Now we're ready for the fun part! Jason,
please sprinkle some flour on the table." Jason did, and then Izzie dropped the dough ball on it.
"Nina, please roll out the dough until it's about six
millimeters thick," Allison said. "I love using rolling pins!" Nina said, rolling
happily. Bobby laughed. "You look like a pizza maker, Nina!" he said. Allison picked up a cookie
cutter shaped like a dog bone. "Everyone, grab a cookie cutter
and start cutting out bones! Press the
cutter into the dough. Wiggle it around and then
lift it up. Then place the bone-shaped dough on
the cookie tray." Jason lined up his dog-bone treats on the
tray. He hoped Lucy liked peanut butter and that no one adopted her before
tomorrow! He couldn't wait to give her a special treat. "Bake the treats for forty minutes," Allison told the
campers. "I have to go back to the shelter now. But I'll
see you tomorrow. Don't forget to bring the treats!" "Bye, Allison! Thank you!" The campers
waved good-bye. The next day the campers arrived at Penny's with dog bones. Jason
looked down the row of cages. He spotted his favorite dog right away.
"Lucy!" he cried. "Here's a peanut butter treat.
Just for you!" Things you'll need: - 2 cups whole wheat
flour - 1 cup rolled oats - cooking spray - 1/3 cup
peanut butter - 1 ¼ cup hot water - dog bone cookie
cutter (or any other cookie cutter) Do It Yourself: 1) Preheat the oven to 175 degrees Celsius. 2) Mix
the flour and oats in a large bowl. 3) Spray the
measuring cup with cooking spray and measure out the peanut butter. 4) Combine the
peanut butter and hot water in a small bowl. Stir until the
peanut butter melts and the mixture
is smooth. 5) Combine the wet and dry
ingredients. Knead dough into a ball.
Add more flour if necessary.
6) Using a rolling pin, roll the dough out to 6 mm thickness. 7)
Using the cookie cutter, cut the dough into dog bones.
8) Place the bones on a cookie sheet and
bake for forty minutes.
9) Allow to cool completely before serving
to your favorite furry
friend!
Izzie knew the campers were doing something messy today. The picnic table
was covered with garbage bags. And Mr. Dunn was wearing an apron
and rubber gloves. "Great!" Izzie thought. Messy meant fun! "It looks like Laundry
Day," Bobby said. He pointed
to a bucket of
water filled with T-shirts. "Nope," Mr. Dunn said with
a smile. "It's Tie-dyed T-shirt Day!" Mr. Dunn held up a blue and green
T-shirt. It was tie-dyed and had the words "Kids Central
Summer Camp" on it. "Awesome!" Izzie
cried. "I want that shirt! I'm going to make one exactly like
it." "Grab your aprons and a pair of gloves, campers," said Mr. Dunn. "You don't want the dye
getting on your skin or clothes. Only on the shirt
you're dying!" Mr. Dunn chuckled. "Start by choosing a T-shirt from
the bucket." Mr. Dunn showed the campers how to wring the water out of the shirts.
"Now we're ready to make our designs," he said. "Can anyone guess how I made mine?"
Izzie studied his shirt. She also saw rubber bands on the table.
"You put rubber bands around the T-shirt before you dyed it!"
Izzie said. "The dye couldn't get under the rubber bands. That's why there are those white stripes!" Mr. Dunn smiled.
"Good thinking, Izzie." "First twist your shirt," the teacher said. "Then make
sections with rubber bands. Each rubber band will become a
white stripe. To make a
pattern of circles, twist the middle section of the shirt. Add
rubber bands to make rings around your circle." "I want stripes, just like yours, Mr. Dunn," Izzie said.
"I'm making circles," said Nina. The boys chose circles too. "Now it's
time to dye. Carefully squeeze dye onto each section."
Mr. Dunn demonstrated. "You can use just two colors,
or as many as you want," Mr. Dunn said.
Izzie looked at Mr. Dunn's shirt. It had green
stripes at the top and blue ones at the bottom. Izzie
used those colors too. "Now put the shirts in plastic bags. The dye needs to soak in for
the rest of the day," said Mr. Dunn. "At home you'll have
to hang up the shirts to let them dry." The kids set their bagged
shirts aside. But Izzie wasn't good at
waiting. She wanted to see her shirt
now . "Can we peek at the
shirts, to check our designs?" she asked. "No."
Mr. Dunn shook his
head. "You have to wait, Izzie." "Waiting is so hard," Izzie thought. What if she had made a mistake? What if
her shirt didn't come out like Mr. Dunn's?
Finally the teacher announced, "It's time!" The kids rushed back to their shirts. Izzie thought the other campers'
shirts looked great. Then she took hers
out of the bag. She gasped. There were only two
green stripes and five blue ones. "Mr. Dunn, it doesn't look like your shirt at all!" she cried. "It's much better
than my shirt," Mr. Dunn said. "The uneven pattern is beautiful! You'll see how great it looks when
we all wear our shirts on Friday." Izzie smiled. Now
she couldn't wait until Friday! Things you’ll need:
- a cotton T-shirt - water - a bucket -
garbage bags - masking tape - rubber bands - plastic squeeze bottles - 2 or 3
colors of fabric dye - large sealable plastic
bags - latex or rubber gloves Do
It Yourself: 1) Soak your T-shirt in water. 2)
Prepare the different colors of fabric dye in separate
squeeze bottles. Follow the instructions on the dye package. 3) Tape garbage bags over
your workspace. This is a messy craft! 4) Wring
out your T-shirt to remove excess water. Twist it
into one long roll to make stripes. Twist just one section
near the middle to make circles instead. 5) Put rubber bands
around your twisted shirt to make as many stripes or circles as you want. 6) Using a
squeeze bottle, squeeze dye onto each section. 7) Place your T-shirt into a sealable plastic bag and
let it sit for a few hours or overnight. 8) Remove your
T-shirt from the bag and take off
the rubber bands. Hang up the shirt to dry. 9) Wash your T-shirt thoroughly (once or twice) to make sure
all the extra dye comes off. 10) Wear your new, personally-designed
T-shirt!
Plop ! A drop of sweat fell from Jason's forehead. It
landed right on his video game. "Ugh. It's so
hot!" Mr. Dunn pointed at
Jason's game. "That needs to go away. We're
about to head inside to make
some food." "We're cooking on this hot, hot day?" Jason asked.
"I hope we're not using the oven!" Bobby cried. Mr. Dunn chuckled.
"Don't worry. We're making cold cucumber pickles. Perfect for today." "That's
no fun. Pickles have to sit
around in jars for a long time.
We won't get to
eat them today!"
Jason frowned. "We're making instant pickles." Mr. Dunn winked. "Have you ever made those?"
Jason shook his head. "We should get started. The process has a
few steps. But I promise they'll be ready
to eat by the end of the
day." Mr. Dunn clapped his
hands. "It's pickle time!" Inside
the gym it was still hot. But
Jason was glad there was a fan. "Look at all those cucumbers!" Ethan cried. "They're from my garden,"
Mr. Dunn said proudly. "So how
do we turn cucumbers
into pickles?" Izzie asked. "First choose a cucumber from
the basket," said Mr. Dunn. "Yay! We each get our
own!" Nina picked the smallest one. "There's a cutting
board and knife for each of you. Carefully slice your
cucumbers as thin as possible. Place the slices in the bowls of salt
water," Mr. Dunn instructed. Jason carefully followed the teacher's instructions. "We'll leave
our slices there and prepare the pickle juice."
Mr. Dunn motioned for everyone to
follow him to the next table. Nina looked confused. "Pickle juice is the
liquid you put pickles in," Jason whispered. Nina smiled thankfully.
"The juice is eight tablespoons rice vinegar," read Bobby. "And one and a half tablespoons
sugar," Ethan continued. "Plus one teaspoon salt,"
Izzie added. "And four tablespoons of boiling water!" Nina said. The kids each
made their own jar of pickle juice. When they were done, Mr. Dunn reminded them
about their cucumbers. "It's
time to drain them. One at a time now at the sink." "Here's the

extra water out of the slices with your hands. Just like
you're wringing a towel. Grab a bunch and squeeze. Then pat

the cucumbers in the pickle juice?" he asked. Mr. Dunn
nodded. "Sure is." "It's twelve
o'clock now. Our pickles will be ready at three." Mr. Dunn looked around at
the hot, sweaty faces. "That's just enough
time for a quick trip to the
air-conditioned town library." "Hooray!" Everyone cheered. Later the campers returned to the gym. The
pickles were waiting. The campers drained the juice and then grabbed
forks. A cold mouthful of pickles tickled as it
slid down Jason's throat. "Yum! Instant pickles are my new favorite food!"
Things you’ll need: - 1 medium-sized cucumber - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 1
cup water - paper towels For the pickle juice: - 8 tablespoons rice vinegar - 1 ½ tablespoons
sugar - 1 teaspoon salt -
4 tablespoons boiling water Do
It Yourself: 1) Add 1/2 teaspoon salt to 1

Ethan was thinking hard as he walked to the playground. It was almost
the end of summer camp, and he was sad. He didn't know if he'd see Mr. Dunn
after camp was over. He wanted to give Mr. Dunn something that would show how much
everyone liked camp. He wanted it to be something that would help Mr. Dunn to remember everyone. "Hey, Ethan," Mr.
Dunn said cheerfully. "Did you bring your empty soda bottle?" Ethan pulled a bottle out of his backpack. "What
is it for?" "We're going to use it
to make a terrarium." Mr. Dunn held up a
package of seeds. "Has anyone ever heard of a terrarium?" he
asked. "Ooh, my pet frog,
Gurpy, lives in a terrarium! Wow! Are we growing frogs, Mr. Dunn?
Are we?" Izzie asked excitedly. Mr. Dunn laughed. "Terrariums can be
for animals or plants. We're going to plant seeds in our bottles.

we need to get some pebbles and soil." Mr. Dunn
held up large paper cups. "Let's
head to the woods." Mr. Dunn pointed to the ground underneath a tree. "Here's
a good place to get soil." Ethan stuck a cup into
the soil. "Is it okay
if we scoop up worms?" "A soda bottle
is a pretty small home for a worm," Mr. Dunn said. "Let's leave
the worms out here in the woods." Ethan nodded. Mr.
Dunn always had good answers. The kids
were ready to create their terrariums. "First we have to cut our
bottles," said Mr. Dunn. "We're going to use the
bottom part for planting." He told the campers to
draw a line on the bottle. "Make it about 12 centimeters
from the bottom." "Mr. Dunn likes to garden," Ethan thought. Maybe the campers could get Mr. Dunn a shovel.
How much did shovels cost? Mr. Dunn helped everyone cut their bottles.
Then they were ready for pebbles and soil. "Place one layer
of pebbles on the bottom of your terrarium. Then fill the
terrarium with soil. Leave about four centimeters of room at the top," said
Mr. Dunn. "Then add seeds. You can grow grass, clover, or basil."
Ethan followed Mr. Dunn's instructions. He sprinkled a handful of clover seeds in his terrarium
and covered them with soil. "Now lightly water your seeds with
a spray bottle. Don't soak the soil. It only
needs to be moist," Mr. Dunn said. "I actually lost my watering
can at home. So I've been watering
my indoor plants with this spray bottle!" Mr. Dunn
said. "That's it!" Ethan thought. A watering can would be the
perfect gift from the Kids Central kids! The campers fitted the top halves of their
bottles back on their terrariums. Ethan thought about
his idea for Mr. Dunn's gift. The last day of camp was going to be sad.

Mr. Dunn the watering can, everyone would be happy!
Things you’ll need: - a plastic 2-liter
bottle with cap - a permanent marker - sharp scissors or craft knife - pebbles - potting soil - seeds
(herbs, grasses, and African violets all grow well in terrariums) - water
Do It Yourself: 1) Remove the
label from your bottle. Wash and dry the bottle and cap. 2)
Draw a line around your bottle, about 12 centimeters from the
bottom. 3) With a grown-up's help, cut the bottle on the line. 4) In the bottom part of
the bottle, place one layer of
pebbles. 5) Fill the rest of the bottom part with soil. Be sure to leave about four
centimeters at the top. 6) Plant a few seeds in the soil. Cover lightly with soil. 7) Water
seeds with a spray bottle. 8) Fit the top half of the
bottle back onto the bottom. Keep the cap on the bottle. 9) Put
your terrarium in a sunny spot and watch your plant grow! Continue to water with spray bottle as
needed.
Bobby grinned when he arrived at camp on Friday. All the
campers, including Mr. Dunn, were wearing their tie-dyed T-shirts. "We look like a team!"

Sweet Iced Lemonade (see Fun at Kids Central Episode 52) - a cooler filled with

- a money box
- cardboard or paper (for the

It Yourself: 1)
Prepare Sweet Iced Lemonade. Fill a cooler with ice to serve with the lemonade. 2) Set up a table with
paper cups, a money box,

what you're selling and how much

customers!

Things you’ll need: - white paper for the quilt squares - construction paper in different colors for the
shapes - scissors - a large sheet of mural paper
- pencils - glue Do It Yourself: 1) Spread the mural paper on the floor. With

sad. Bobby was playing soccer, so he

handprints and take photos," Miss Shelly said.

question. What do you want to learn this year?" "How to build

." Bobby looked up. On the table Ethan had

Do It Yourself: 1) Chop the raisins in
the food processor. Transfer to a bowl. 2) Chop the nuts
in the food processor and add to the bowl. 3) Add melted butter to

yarn (cut into 90 centimeters pieces) - wooden sticks -

size of your pumpkin. 2) Tie a piece of

." "What's

tablespoon cheongju (cooking rice wine) - salt and
pepper - 2 tablespoons gochujang (red pepper paste) - 1/4 cup ketchup - 2 tablespoons honey - 1 tablespoon
soy sauce - 2 teaspoons sesame oil - 1 clove
garlic, grated - cooking oil spray - skewers
